newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: Costa Rica September inflation rises 0.91 pct.
newsitem.headline: Costa Rica September inflation rises 0.91 pct.

text.p: Costa Rica's consumer price index rose in September by 0.91 percent after rising by 0.96 percent in August, the government said on Thursday.
"The pace of growth in living costs has been declining in a sustained manner," the Minister of Economy, Industry and Trade, Jose Leon Desanti, said at a news conference.
Desanti said that cumulative inflation from January to September of this year was 10.1 percent, down from the 14.93 percent seen in the same period a year earlier.
From September 1995 to September 1996 cumulative inflation was 17.4 percent, the government said.
The increase in September this year was mainly due to an increase in products such as bread, eggs, coffee, sugar, beans and some restaurant meals.
The price of cigarettes and fuels also rose.
Desanti said the government is hoping 1996 inflation won't surpass 12.0 percent.
